subject: D-D: the 79 ASDAN decks measured on both print arms, one deck per family

population.howIdentified: decks under the three ASDAN trees carrying .print-section, START_HERE excluded

armA: load the deck and print it as it stands - what Ctrl+P does with no route chosen
armB: click the deck's own route button first (the harness found '🖨 Supported pack'), then print
result: arm A prints ONE page with zero characters and zero ink, and 0 of 15-16 .print-section elements compute display:block. Arm B prints 5 pages, 5550-6973 characters, ink on 16-17% of the sampled pixels, and 11 of 15-16 sections block - the other 4-5 are the routes not chosen.
verdict: D-D's proof condition is NOT met, and that is the finding. It asks for non-blank on BOTH arms and for EVERY .print-section to compute display:block under print. Arm A is blank and only 11 of 15-16 sections are ever block at once - by design, because the remaining ones belong to the other two routes. The patch D-D would authorise (forcing every .print-section visible under print) would print all three routes at once and would damage 79 decks that currently print correctly. Run 7 reached the same conclusion by a different route and withdrew the finding; this run re-measured it rather than citing it.
realFinding: a teacher who presses Ctrl+P without first choosing a pack gets one wholly blank sheet with no instruction on it. That is a design question for Matt, not a byte-identical patch: the deck could paint a single 'choose a print pack' line, or default the print stylesheet to the supported pack. Either is a ruling, and it is carried to the human items rather than taken.
